hero.tagline: A coding agent that cannot declare itself finished.
hero.lede: Most agent loops end when the model stops calling tools. magi requires the agent to explicitly declare it is done. Three council members then review the record — what ran, real exit codes, and disk changes — before accepting the declaration.
hero.note: Apache-2.0 · Pure Go, single static binary · Runs with Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API
sec.what.head: When does a turn truly end?
sec.what.lede: If a turn ends implicitly when the model stops calling tools, a stalled agent looks identical to a finished one. This causes two common failures: agents stopping halfway, and agents never stopping.
figure.title: A rejected completion claim
figure.caption: The record does not support the agent's claim, so it is sent back to work.
sec.council.head: Three lenses, one decision
sec.council.lede: Where standard loops end, three council members vote done, reject, or abstain. A pure function tallies these votes into a final decision. They all read the same record, but each evaluates it through a different lens and starts looking from a different angle.
council.melchior.walk: The task's exact words (values, formats, names) and the premises of the work.
council.balthasar.walk: The exact moment each required action ran and the actual output it returned.
council.casper.walk: Every distinct requirement requested, even those mentioned only in passing.
council.walk.head: A walk before the verdict
council.walk.body: Before voting, each member checks the requirements line by line. Each is marked SATISFIED or UNSATISFIED based strictly on verbatim tool outputs, or NO-EVIDENCE. This evaluation is placed before the verdict in the schema, preventing retroactive justification. The agent's own summary is ignored.
council.close.head: The closing call
council.close.body: The final tally reads all three reviews. Its decision only clamps in one direction: it can turn a done into a continue, but never the reverse. A gate that can be talked into opening is not a gate.
tally.majority.when: a strict majority of voting members say done; a tie continues
tally.quorum.when: at least k members say done
tally.weighted.when: the done-weight share meets threshold θ
tally.veto.when: a named member can refuse any finish on its own
tally.note: Ambiguous outcomes always resolve to continue. A member that errors, times out, or returns unparseable data simply abstains. Flaky models can weaken the vote but never freeze the loop.
sec.record.head: The record, not the claim
sec.record.lede: Members do not judge the agent by its own summary. They verify against magi's internal record. Because magi executes every tool call, it knows:
record.1: Every command that ran and its true exit code, including which pipe stage failed.
record.2: The exact file edits made during the turn, shown as before-and-after diffs.
record.3: A fresh workspace scan on completion: newly modified files, running background jobs, and paths the agent claims to have written that are missing.
record.line: A predefined test can misunderstand the work. A record of executed commands cannot lie about what ran.
sec.fleet.head: More than one agent
sec.fleet.lede: A magi bound to a workspace is a companion. Give it a role in the project config, and it becomes addressable by its purpose.
fleet.1.b: Lists all companions and what they have learned, making specialists visible to the rest.
fleet.2.b: Hands off a piece of work and carries on. The result arrives in your conversation when finished.
fleet.3.b: Puts several companions in a read-only room to discuss a question until everyone knows their task.
fleet.4.b: Every daemon logs a record beside its socket, which acts as the membership list. Across machines, these records sync over ssh, so magi opens no ports and needs no credentials.
shot.companions.cap: All local companions: their current status and tasks waiting for your input.
shot.detail.cap: A single companion's live transcript with real exit codes and a command pending approval.
shot.meeting.cap: Meetings: multiple companions discuss a problem and produce individual action plans.
shot.board.cap: Tasks organized into cards, separated by team, and grouped by agent-assigned labels.
sec.clients.head: One companion, multiple clients
sec.clients.lede: Clients are external programs that attach to a companion using the same socket. If a client can access the log file, it reads it directly instead of asking the daemon.
seat.terminal.b: magi runs the engine and TUI together. magi --attach connects to an existing daemon in the workspace. magi -p runs a single turn and exits.
seat.console.b: magi-web displays all companions across connected machines on one screen. It binds locally and requires no separate login.
seat.jetbrains.b: An IDE window acts as a companion. The transcript lives in the tool window, and the IDE itself becomes a tool for the agent to read and edit open buffers.
seat.vscode.b: Provides the transcript, plans, approvals, and composer in VS Code, connecting to the same universal socket.
seat.visualstudio.b: The core layer is ready, but the IDE UI is not yet built. It is listed here as a planned addition.
seat.powerpoint.b: The task pane binds to the deck's companion, exposing slide-editing tools via MCP. Every open deck has its own conversation.
seat.excel.b: The identical pane, but controlling sheets, ranges, and formulas instead of slides.
seat.word.b: Applies the same model to paragraphs and styles. All three Office add-ins run from a single process and port.
sec.feature.head: What you get
feature.termination.b: Three members vote on completion. A pure, unit-tested function tallies votes. If rejected, their feedback becomes the next prompt.
feature.walk.b: Requirements are mapped line-by-line to verbatim tool outputs before the schema permits a final vote.
feature.record.b: Logs every command, true exit codes (including failed pipe stages), written files, and scans the workspace on every completion claim.
feature.console.b: Monitor all companions from a browser. You can interrupt tasks, answer questions, approve commands, read their memories, and receive push notifications.
feature.loop.b: Every turn is saved as an event-sourced JSONL log, making operations like /rewind, /fork, /replay, and /loopdiff natively supported.
feature.binaries.b: Built in pure Go with no CGO dependencies. The agent and console are separate static binaries that run anywhere.
feature.companions.b: Assign a role to a workspace to address it by its purpose. Use hand_off to delegate work to specialists while continuing the main task. Meetings align multiple companions on a plan.
feature.knowledge.b: Skills and memories are scoped to a companion, team, or everyone. The shared wiki updates in place, preserving retired pages with context.
feature.tools.b: Includes 24 built-in tools and supports external MCP servers. Editor plugins and add-ins act as temporary MCP servers while open. Lua plugins offer capability bundles.
feature.guard.b: A profile is two axes — permission and sandbox. Secret paths like .env are a floor nothing crosses, and shell commands are read for destruction, egress and pipes into a shell. A delete that aims outside the workspace asks first, and what an edit overwrote is held by a hard link.
feature.complete.b: Provides autocomplete and prompt suggestions based on your history. Uses a lightweight routing profile so typing is never delayed by the agent loop.
feature.update.t: A fleet that keeps itself current
feature.update.b: Daemons securely update themselves by verifying checksums, running a safe rollback pre-flight check, and restarting in-place without losing conversations. Never across machines, never over your own source builds.
sec.start.head: How to start
sec.start.lede: Go 1.26+ to build, and an OpenAI-compatible backend. The default model runs on Ollama's free cloud tier — no GPU, one sign-in — and any local model works too.
start.more: Read the manual for configuration, profiles, sandboxes, plugins, MCP, and managing the fleet.
foot.note: This page is built from the very repository it describes. The demo uses the real console UI backed by browser-side mocks — no server needed.
